# <span id="aanchor57"></span> Group Access

A FLOWCAL group is a list of users that receive all the privileges that have been granted to the group. A user can be a member of multiple groups so that they can gain access to additional meters and/or privileges. User access is determined by the access specified in the user permissions or their group permissions. If access is granted at either the group or the user level, the selected users will have the same access. You must log out and log back in to refresh your privileges.

User security should only be enabled within the User Access screen, not the Group Access screen. FLOWCAL relies on database roles to manipulate users at the database level. Database roles can only be granted to users and not groups.

<div class="procedure">

To access the Group Access screen: 

1.  Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**.
2.  Select groups in the security group.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 550;height: 446;" />

Administrators must have the **Application Process - User Security** privileges to manage user or group IDs.

 

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="General Details">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Group Access Screen Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="General Details">

The following items are available on the Group Access screen:

- **ID** - The security group name.

- **AD Group** - Indicates the Windows Active Directory group associated with the FLOWCAL security group.

  Each FLOWCAL group can only map to a single AD group, but one AD group can be mapped to any number of FLOWCAL groups.

- **System** - Privileges are configured for each group ID for each system. A group ID can have access to multiple systems. For example: A group ID can have view-only privileges on one system and edit privileges on another. Members of a group will only be able to see the systems the group has access to. Access to a system is given by an administrator using the System Manager.

  The default system is "ENTERPRISE," but there could be multiple systems to choose from such as "GAS" or "LIQUID". By selecting a system from the System drop-down box on the User or Group Access screens, security can be defined uniquely within each system for a user or group ID.

  This feature requires the Multi-System Extension module.

- **Group May Access All Meters** - This option allows group members to select any meter within the system. This option only grants the ability to select meters; what the group members can do with the meter data is still restricted by the group’s privileges.

<!-- -->

- **Group May Access All Quality Sources** - This option allows group members to select any quality source within the system. This option only grants the ability to select quality sources; what the group can do with the quality source data is still restricted by the group’s privileges.

<!-- -->

- **Group May Access All Locations** - This option will allow the group members to select any location within the system. This option only grants the ability to select locations; what the group can do with the location data is still restricted by the group’s privileges.

<!-- -->

- **Edit Approval Limits** - Determines the maximum amount of total edits for volume and energy that members of a group can approve for a given month, for each meter.

  - **Custom Limit** - User-defined limits for the maximum PPA or edit the group can approve.
  - **System Limit** - Limits defined within System Configuration screen or System Manager.
  - **No Limit** - No approval limit restrictions are set for this group.

  The group must also have the Edit/PPA Approval - Can Approve privilege.

- **Application Process** - Security options affect all processes across the application for all systems.

- **System Process** - Security settings defined per system.

- **Ticket Access** - Ticket statuses are only populated if the FLOWCAL configuration option to automatically finalize is enabled (this option is only available with FC 8.11.38 and earlier). If this option is enabled, ticket access can be restricted.

- **Check All** - Grant all privileges for all application processes or system processes.

<!-- -->

- **Clear All** - Remove all privileges for all application processes or system processes.
- **Refresh** - Reload the group ID from the database.
- **New** - Create a new group ID.
- **Edit** - Edit an existing group ID.
- **Delete** - Delete a security group ID.
- **Save** - Save changes.
- **Cancel** - Cancel changes.
- **Exit** - Exit the screen.
- **Members** - Launch the Edit Group screen to add/remove members for the security group selected.
- **Notes** - Add notes for a given security group ID.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="App Process Details">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Application Process Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="App Process Details">

The following items are available in the Application Process section of the Group Access screen:

- **Close Groups** - Grant access to create, edit, and delete close groups.
- Data Archive - Grant access to view and edit data archive-related settings.
- **FLOWCAL Options** - Grant access to several groupings within the Settings Manager screen (e.g. Services, Application Geographic, and Liquids).
- **Personality** - Allow toggle between FLOWCAL and TESTit using the **Ctl+T** functionality. (Applicable to TESTit Integrated v2 only.)
- **System** - Grant access to create, edit, and delete systems from the System Manager.
- **TESTit Admin** - Grant access to the administrative features under the TESTit Manager menu ( TESTit Options, Data Map Editor, and some administrative menus under TESTit Scheduler).
- **Ticket Autofill** - Grant access to set up defaults for ticket fields.
- **User Security** - Grant access to User/Group Access within FLOWCAL.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="System Process Details">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />System Process Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="System Process Details">

The following items are available in the System Process section of the Group Access screen:

- **Data Transfer** - Import and export privileges control access to the Data Transfer module within FcDataBoss.
- **Meter Edit - Can Delete** - This privilege is commonly withheld from users that are limited to day-to-day processing.
- **Purge - Historical Purge** - Historical purge privilege controls access to the Historical Purge module in FcDataBoss.

</div>

Run the [User Roles and Privileges](../../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/Editor%20Reports.md#User) report to view the privileges for each user ID based on user and group permissions.
